classification.difficultyReason: Multiply probabilities for independent replacement draws and combine mutually exclusive orders or colour cases.

content.prompt: A bag contains 15 blue balls and 10 green balls. A ball is taken out and its colour noted. It is replaced. A second ball is taken out and its colour noted. Find the probability of obtaining:

children.label: a
children.prompt: a green ball followed by a blue ball

answer.worked:
Replacement makes the draws independent.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{green then blue})&=\frac{10}{25}\times\frac{15}{25}\\P(\text{green then blue})&=\frac{6}{25}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: a green and a blue ball

answer.worked:
The colours can occur in either order. Add the probabilities of these mutually exclusive outcomes.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{one of each})&=\frac{10}{25}\times\frac{15}{25}+\frac{15}{25}\times\frac{10}{25}\\P(\text{one of each})&=\frac{6}{25}+\frac{6}{25}\\P(\text{one of each})&=\frac{12}{25}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: two balls of the same colour

answer.worked:
The balls are either both green or both blue. These outcomes are mutually exclusive.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{same colour})&=\frac{10}{25}\times\frac{10}{25}+\frac{15}{25}\times\frac{15}{25}\\P(\text{same colour})&=\frac{4}{25}+\frac{9}{25}\\P(\text{same colour})&=\frac{13}{25}\end{align*}$$
